blocks.value: Unlike a Market Order, a Limit Order lets you decide the exact price at which you want to buy or sell a share.

Imagine This: You visit a shop to buy a mobile phone. The shopkeeper asks ₹20,000, but you say, 'I'll buy it only if the price drops to ₹18,500.' You leave your offer and wait. A Limit Order works exactly like that.
Your order will only be executed if the market reaches the price you specified. Otherwise, the order remains pending or expires.
A stock is trading at ₹1,020. You place a Limit Buy Order at ₹1,000. Your order will execute only if someone is willing to sell at ₹1,000.
Use Limit Orders when getting the right price is more important than immediate execution.

blocks.question: When does a Limit Order execute?
choices: Only when the specified price is reached.
